standards.text: databases and database management systems store, organize, and manage data efficiently, and that relational and nonrelational models serve different purposes in real-world applications across various industries.

Structured Query Language (SQL) is an essential tool for creating, managing, and manipulating data in databases, and that SQL concepts such as tables, rows, columns, syntax structures, and data types support the effective organization and processing of information.

SQL commands enable data to be queried, modified, aggregated, grouped, filtered, and combined across tables, allowing meaningful information to be retrieved from databases through well-structured executable queries.
the basic concepts of databases and SQL, including queries, functions, and commands, enable effective database management and manipulation.
The learners utilize basic database concepts, SQL functions, and SQL commands to perform database management tasks.
The learners use basic database concepts, SQL functions, and SQL commands to design simple databases.

competencies.text: define database and database management system.
differentiate relational and non-relational databases, their purposes and functions.
discuss real-world applications of databases and database management system.
explain the basic concepts of SQL and its role in data management and analysis.
explain the concepts of tables, rows, and columns in a database.
create an Entity–Relationship (ER) Diagram representing entities, attributes, and relationships in a relational database.
explain the roles of primary keys and foreign keys in establishing and maintaining relationships between database tables.
identify key components of SQL syntax and common SQL data types.
create databases and tables using SQL, including inserting and updating data.
differentiate SQL command structures based on their purpose and usage in data definition, data manipulation, and data querying.
write executable queries against a database using an appropriate SQL command.
identify the structure of a SQL command statement
explain how SQL clauses are used to filter results.
write executable queries against a database using appropriate SQL commands.
develop a database management system using SQL.
present the developed database management system before an audience.
